reviews.text:
Seems designed to take advantage of the people it says it will help. 

I don’t normally write reviews, but in this case my experience was so bad, that it seemed necessary in case it could help someone else avoid the same distress. 

Paid for a trial and didn’t know it was set to auto renew. NO WARNING  that renewal was going to happen and payment would soon be taken. Suddenly had £95 taken from my account. Contacted them within even an hour of the payment notification on my bank account, on the exact day it renewed, and received a bot/copy & paste response simply quoting policy. Emailed them back and received the same again. 

From the other reviews I can see that many people have had the same experience, which should indicate to the developers that there is a fundamental issue in the way their customer accounts work.

Utterly disgusting behaviour. For an app that states it will lessen stress and anxiety, it has done nothing but increase it.

I’m going to predict that I will receive a response to this review that will again quote policy, indicate that they are ‘Sorry for the experience’, and ‘Will review it again if I email them again’, which will get me nowhere. The responses to the other reviews are extremely patronising, with unhelpful information. I expect I will get the same.

I would also like to point out how ironic it is that people who have had this experience are being asked to write to an email address that includes the word ‘trust.’ How horrendously poetic.

A word of warning to anyone considering Liven: read the small print carefully and make sure you know exactly when your subscription renews and at what price.

I initially subscribed at a discounted rate of £47.99, only to be automatically charged £95.99 after 12 weeks. I received no advance renewal notification and later discovered that reminders need to be enabled within the app.

What disappointed me most was the customer service. When I contacted Liven directly to request a goodwill refund, or even a partial one, I was repeatedly referred back to the terms and conditions, with no flexibility despite their policy allowing discretionary refunds.

For an app promoting emotional wellbeing, self-awareness and personal growth, I find this lack of understanding particularly disappointing.

My advice: check your renewal date, enable reminders yourself and be aware that customer service may offer little beyond repeating the subscription policy.

reviews.title: Beware of Liven’s Separate Subscriptions and Misleading Cancellation Process
reviews.text:
I signed up for Liven in October 2025 and canceled my subscription directly through the app in November 2025. I even received an email confirming the cancellation. Despite this, Liven continued charging me for nearly a year without my knowledge.

When I discovered the charges and contacted customer support, I was told that Liven apparently maintains two separate subscriptions: one for the app and another for the website. According to their support team, I had canceled the app subscription but not the website subscription.

Here’s the problem: I’ve never used their website, never logged into it, and don’t even have a website login to my knowledge. I canceled my subscription through the very app I signed up with and received written confirmation. Any reasonable customer would assume that meant their subscription was canceled and the billing would stop.

Instead of acknowledging how misleading and confusing this arrangement is, Liven has refused to refund the charges, insisting that I failed to cancel a separate subscription I didn’t even know existed.

Dealing with their support team has been equally frustrating. I’ve had to repeatedly explain the same basic facts, to the point that I genuinely cannot tell whether I’m communicating with an AI system incapable of understanding the issue or poorly trained representatives who lack the authority to resolve it. I’ve now had to threaten a credit card dispute and a formal consumer protection complaint just to get this taken seriously.

I initially paid £8.32, which felt like a fair and reasonable price for the service. After that period, however, I was charged £48 for just 28 days of access — effectively putting the app at around £600 per year.

I accept that I should have cancelled the subscription, but I think there is a significant difference between a customer making a minor oversight and a company charging such an enormous amount as a result. The jump from £8.32 to £48 is completely disproportionate to the product and feels designed to profit from people forgetting to cancel.

For an app whose purpose is supposedly to help people with organisation and managing their lives, relying on users overlooking a subscription renewal feels particularly questionable.

I would have happily paid the original rate, but £48 every 28 days is simply not a reasonable reflection of the value of this app. The product may be useful, but the pricing strategy is, in my opinion, exploitative and seriously undermines my trust in the company.

reviews.text: don’t do it. you can’t even check out the app without putting in your credit card info and then when you go to open up the app it forces you to answer questions. no way to get to settings without answering questions. it also doesn’t show up in your apple subscriptions to easily cancel. so then once your free period is up you get charged because you totally forgot about the app because you were never able to use it in the first place without putting in information that you didn’t want to give to get past to “supposedly” get to a settings option. DO NOT RECOMMEND

reviews.title: Scammy and almost impossible to cancel
reviews.text: The content on this app is interesting and useful, but it is presented as a lot of dense text and quite exhausting to read sometimes. They’ve tried to make it more engaging by encouraging the user to keep coming back and getting multi-day streaks, when the incentive should be because the app is engaging to use. The real reason why I am giving it such a low rating is because it is almost impossible to cancel your subscription. You have to jump through so many hoops that it almost feels like a scam. Also the whole time you are using it they try to upsell you to the next package. I would not recommend. Even with their “free gifts” - you will always end up paying.

reviews.title: Lame
reviews.text: Waste of money. I don’t need a journal I pay for.

reviews.title: Annoying pop ups all the time
reviews.text: Every time I click on something and return to the home page, this pop up begging me for a review shows up. And the app is constantly trying to upsell me

reviews.title: Caution: Quiz Not A Diagnostic Tool
reviews.text: Speaking for myself as a nuerodiverse individual there was in retrospect no need for me to bother enough with even the three minute quiz. I found the questions were too broad and overlapping with other conditions to be effective or helpful. It was another self diagnosis slip and slide that clouds the territory through the trap of self conviction. Considering ADHD has a 70% comorbid rate as of the time of this review, Livens choice to leave vital core principles and information off the table while taking people’s money was and remains difficult not to take as anything short of predatory.  The bottom line:  I see fins in the water that don’t look like dolphins. I’m not a marine biologist but I’m not pretending to be one either.

reviews.title: Poor Ethics
reviews.text: I hate to post this review because I like many things about this app.  However I have discovered from speaking to the support chat that some features offered are in “testing” and don’t work no matter what you do.  I think this is a hugely unethical practice because if someone in crisis used the app and couldn’t understand why certain features don’t work it could exacerbate the crisis. Professional ethics including informed consent should still be applicable even on a mental health app.

reviews.title: Difficult app to cancel
reviews.text: I’m still getting charged $38 for this app because you have to go through forced steps within the app to cancel. The subscription does not show up in the App Store. I find this sneaky to get people’s money.

reviews.title: This App would not allow me to progress
reviews.text: I would put “minus” stars if I could. I signed up and paid for this app with so much hope. A few clicks in, it greyed out the “Continue” button and would not let me progress. The support team were absolutely useless, sending me irritating placatory messages, but over two weeks, they were completely unable to get the App to work for me. I suggested that they cancel and then re-start the whole thing for me - but apparently that is not possible. They tell me (via emails) that they do not ever telephone or speak to a customer. Their technical team concluded that no, their App would not work for me - without telling me WHY. My IT Manager husband is very curious to know why!

reviews.title: Not helpful
reviews.text: I signed up to try for a few days, didn’t like it, and cancelled. Then this company charged me $40 last week! I haven’t used this app at all and was not subscribed to my knowledge. Cancelled again. It better take this time.

reviews.title: Scammy business practices
reviews.text: When you subscribe, nowhere does it clearly show that it is for three months. On top of that when a renewal comes up, they charge triple the original price. When I inquired about that, they told me that you need to go into settings in order to turn on the auto-renewal reminders 😂. Avoid if you don’t want to get scammed.

reviews.title: Read This Before Subscribing to Liven
reviews.text:
I only purchased the introductory plan to try the app. Afterward, I checked my Apple App Store subscriptions but couldn't find any active subscription, so I genuinely believed there would be no automatic renewal. I later discovered that the subscription was managed through the company's website instead, and I was unexpectedly charged.

The cancellation process was also more complicated than expected. Although the company eventually reviewed my case and issued a full refund, I believe the subscription and renewal process should be much more transparent. Please make it clearer where subscriptions are managed and how users can cancel them before they are charged.

reviews.title: Terrible app and worse customer service.
reviews.text: Absolutely no way to speak to a human at this company. Overpriced, not useful and AI bot Sarah malfunctions.

reviews.title: If I could give zero stars I would
reviews.text: This app is a scam. “Customer support” is AI assistants, I tried to cancel the app and it somehow didn’t process that then billed $94.85 and the ai would not put me through to an actual person and would not issue the refund even though it was less than 2 weeks after the erroneous charge. The app was useless and unhelpful.

reviews.title: Scam? Subscription price is WILD
reviews.text: I don’t even understand how I got signed up for a $95/ month subscription because I can assure I would not willingly sign up for that much to ANY subscription. $30 for one time access, fine, but $95?? No, no way. I cancelled and then got an offer to keep for less. I declined. I messaged with customer service (with screenshots) to ensure that I cancelled this scam of an app. The ai chat bot then offers me to keep the subscription for $8/month…. How are you going to go from charging me $95 to $24 for the exact same services?? The ai chat bot answer? “It’s simple: this was a special offer created specifically for you”. So again, definitely a scam. I cancelled today, if I get charged again, I have screenshots to prove I did not want to be subscribed.

reviews.title: Purposefully difficult for unsuspecting vulnerable people
reviews.text: Please don’t get this app if you’re struggling. I got this app with the hope of helping me in a bad time, and I wish I never did. The app in general wasn’t great so over time I forgot about this. For over three months I had zero communication or reminders to use the app or to cancel the subscription. They then took £53 out of my account. When I flagged this with them, the said refunds were on available in the first billing cycle. I think this is really poor form. Preying on the vulnerable in need of help, counting on them to forget to cancel (which is a common factor of mental health issues) and all you’re paying for is AI which you can use ChatGPT for a fraction of the cost. DO NOT get this app.

reviews.title: Poor service
reviews.text: The idea of the app is promising, yet the content doesn’t deliver! Not engaging enough to form any habits or draw you back. This is supported by poor customer service! Most apps offer membership renewal as standard, not with Liven, you have to turn that on manually, and when you try to cancel the subscription it tries every trick in the sales book to make it as difficult as possible with offer after offer, which you have to work through to finally cancel. At just under £50 per month it’s a total rip off and the customer service is as poor as the product!

reviews.title: Scam for people struggling
reviews.text: I downloaded this at a low point in life. I have ADHD and so know what I’m like with subscriptions - I tried to cancel on Apple subscriptions and it’s not on there and so I tried to do it on the app and couldn’t find were to. Fast forward 3 months and no reminders at all and it has renewed at over £50 for a 1/4 I haven’t even logged in for nearly 3 months and really won’t use it now. I feel it takes advantage of people already struggling if it’s so good remind people about the renewal like other apps eg/ Duolingo, don’t con them. It’s told me all I need to know about how good their app really is

reviews.title: Money grabbing
reviews.text:
Was not aware I signed up to a subscription. Showed proof that I had never made an account and therefore never accessed / used their application over an unknown 4 months subscription. As soon as I was aware I emailed the support team and explained the situation. 

Same answer as the other negative reviews I’ve now read. ‘All stated in their terms and conditions - nothing they can do to refund’

I thought this app was supposed to support mental health? Instead it has caused me much grief with over £100 lost on an app I have never used.

I would understand if I had accessed the services but I would have thought a company aimed at supporting mental health would of considered and understood the situation and showed a level of compassion to the situation and offered a refund once proof was given showing I had never used the app or any of its services. Shows it is all about money grabbing and not actually to support people. 

Be careful when even looking at this app - I apparently subscribed when downloaded it before I even made an account as I did not have an account until I had to make one to cancel the unknown subscription.

reviews.title: Wouldn’t recommend based on my experience
reviews.text: I originally signed up for £20 but after a few months increase to above £50! With no warning and because the app didn’t appear in my subscription list I had no idea it was still active until payment was taken! As soon as I had realised I contacted support and I’m not happy with how things have been handled.  Point blank refusing any sort of refund said it was their policy and in their terms and conditions that the increase would happen!! So just be wary, log in and cancel the subscription.  The app is that good I never used it!

reviews.title: Scam - do not download
reviews.text: I paid for a discounted trail and cancelled when I realised it was not useful for me.  Then a few months later realised that payments were still coming out of my account.  I had to download the app again, as I had removed it after I cancelled.  I tried to log on but had forgot my password so had to click password reset request.  The app said an email would be sent with a link.  An email was sent to me saying that my account had been cancelled, no password reset. So it would seem that my account cancellation had not been processed correctly and only completed when I tried to log in again.  I queried this with Liven and have got a response that it was my fault and therefore not refund of my money.  They did not send any emails before I noticed to inform me that money was being taken.  Absolute scam as you can see from other reviews on this.  So disgusted that this is a so called app to help people but it actually takes advantage of people!  Do not try even for a trial unless you want to lose money!!!

reviews.title: Taking advantage of people that struggle
reviews.text: Not gonna lie, this app seemed promising! Seemed like they care. But no, instead, they sell you this “great” four-week plan for £15, but what they miss is that they make you sign up to a subscription turning to £30,99 after the four-week plan. Not only that the app never sent me one single notification as it promises to do…promising that it will encourage you to achieve your best self in these 4 weeks….their customer service is dreadful!!! They have what it seems either AI-generated responses or templates, which shows how this company lacks any real compassion. I couldn’t even get through a real person to talk to and get a refund. They also make it very difficult to unsubscribe from this forced subscription. Would not recommend at all

reviews.title: They don’t care
reviews.text:
Tried the app, it didn’t help me, no warning when trial would end like other apps, charged money even though I thought I had cancelled it, if I had of been warned I would of seen it hasn’t worked, same day charged I explained I did not want to carry on with trial and had tried to cancel , didn’t care about my mental health when. I asked for refund. Now stressed and have a lot of pressure as money was taken. An app that meant to care about your mental health and They don’t care, they only care about money.

Update. Don’t know why you’re saying to message and you will look into it as the emails I have had you are not interested and refused to. Enjoy your money as it only what you want and not to help people.

Update again. Told to contact to but it’s all for show done nothing. Nothing changed. They don’t care

reviews.title: Very disappointed
reviews.text:
I was disappointed by how this app was advertised. It gave the impression that it was free, but after signing up I found that I had to enter my credit card details before I could actually use it. To me, that isn’t what most people understand as “free.”

A free trial that requires payment details and then relies on users remembering to cancel feels misleading. I believe this should be made much clearer before people invest their time in downloading and setting up the app.

The concept of the app seems interesting, but the sign-up experience left me feeling frustrated and misled rather than excited to use it. I hope the developers will consider being more transparent about the subscription process.

reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text: After falling for the ads, I downloaded the app and very soon realised it wasn’t for me, far too uninspiring in its very never ending questions. I thought I had deleted the account. It seems not and a few months on, after not using the app, nearly £60 was taken from my account on Friday. No notification of this upcoming payment was given and on questioning it via chat online over the weekend, have been told that according to the (backward company/business model “it’s in the terms and conditions” and they cannot refund me. I had to have told them by the Thursday, even though I didn’t know I still had an account. Really, really poor, cut-throat customer service experience.  Shame on you to be professing an app to help with mental health and then this is how you conduct your business. And then happy to offer 80% off when trying to close the account (there are multiple layers to this action), so why not just refund me 80% of the money you’ve taken for a service I’m not and haven’t been using! So disappointed in angry … if I could give zero I would. Capitalising on neurodiversity when professing to support.  So bad! AVOID

reviews.title: Mostly good, but not good enough
reviews.text: Let me first say, for the most part, Liven is an okay app. The overall options are good, though, some of the topics and videos and articles are a bit contrived and lacking in solid depth. But good enough. What tipped the scale for me from good enough to ridiculous is the fact that I must contact customer service to start a new journey in the app. Even though I  finished the journey, I have no options or further instructions on what to do to start a new one. I finally, after a couple weeks of the last lesson being completed and sitting in my daily to do dashboard, I contacted customer service who told me I need to go to them to change it. They further told me that not only can they not “disclose” the full list of journey options, I have to tell them what I’d like to explore so they can unlock a journey. How in the world would I know what journey I want to take without a list of options. They could even have me fill out a questionnaire to determine the next journey, instead of having to contact a random customer service agent who is very likely not a counselor or trained mental health professional. As such, I am not only getting rid of the app and going elsewhere, I felt it necessary to leave this review.

reviews.title: Repetitive and frustrating
reviews.text:
This started off ok. The “Journey” lessons were informative but nothing you couldn’t find in a quick internet search. There are only so many and after that I reached out to customer service and they just reset me to the beginning. Like what?!? I paid for a year and this was only a month in. 
The AI chat bot was mediocre at best. It’s clearly designed to end everything in a question to keep you engaged without giving actual practical guidance. 
The “Practice” elements were repetitive and therefore ineffective. I’m someone who actively hates to-do lists and there was no way to skip that. To each their own but I don’t need to add “brush your teeth” to a task list. Super annoying. 
The quizzes have a little insight but I got the same quiz for the third time within the month. Really… why… I can see after like 6 months to redo something and see progress but ummm within a month to have the same thing 3 times?! Nope. 
Overall great in concept but very limited in practice. Have contacted customer service yet again…

reviews.title: Barnum Effect.  Preys on ignorance, has no depth nor specificity
reviews.text:
I can see how someone needing structure and who has never had space for self reflection could benefit from a structured, 3 step, daily routine.  But aside from that, the app is gimmicky and suggests it is doing background personalisation at every loading screen.  I enter positive values and it still insists on suggesting a need for regulation and this app.  
In short, it catches an enormous number of false positives and is probably awful at screening out those without ADHD. But it is a business after all, so the be expected.  Had it said, you’re actually doing great.  Would you like to journal anyway, or do some mindfulness to reinforce the good things going on, that would show they aren’t just a predatory app pouring fuel on the fire of user doubt and ignorance.

Largely text based and not particularly deep, nor interactive.  A good example of the Barnum effect operating inside an incentive-driven business model. The profiling from their test - with focus on things like self-doubt, people-pleasing etc. - is generic enough to apply to a large proportion of people and specific enough to feel personal.  On top of that, this business is commercially structured to produce false positives rather than false negatives. The Harvard, Cambridge and Oxford logos (actually just text, not logos) are credential laundering and a  red flag: proximity implies endorsement without asserting it and this seems like a deliberate ambiguity.

reviews.title: Takes your money time and data
reviews.text: I must have been feeling quite desperate and hoping there was something new out there to help me. But after I entered a lot of personal details and spent some days logging my mood, I didn’t see where it was going. I already have a psychology degree and have meditated 20 years. I just always hope something new will be discovered that can help so I keep trying things. I got nothing out of this. I disabled notifications because I would be interrupted doing things proactively to improve my life, with this app asking me how I’m feeling, which reminded me I feel bad. And because I disabled notifications I forgot the app was there. I thought I could stop the subscription renewing by entering card details of a card I hardly use, then freezing the card. But that doesn’t work. So I paid a month without noticing. I only happened to be awake late at night on the next renewal date, and I saw a pending payment to the liven. I could hardly remember what it was. I went to the app and cancelled my subscription right away, which is a process they make slightly difficult on purpose. I know this because I am a software developer and an expert in user interface design. It is so sad that companies look to exploit people at their worst moments, when they are not functioning as well as normal like me, and just take money and data. I had to wait in a queue in the middle of the night to talk to support to stop the pending change for this month. And I’m writing this review because I can’t go to bed jus

reviews.title: Do not fall for this
reviews.text: Do not fall for this app! Their customer service is horrible. I did the trial and the sign up that makes you agree to being charged 94$ for 3 months. As soon, and I mean immediately when the charge came through I contacted them for a refund to which they refused and then they finally agreed to 50%…. For an app/service that I am not using. Not once did I ever get an email that my trial was expiring (because why would they do that everyone would cancel and not get tricked in to the expensive charge). Since cancellation I have received numerous emails about coming back for 80% off!! What a joke! When someone ask to cancel immediately, a full refund should be issued. Shame on them for keeping your money for something not being used!! Customer service should be better than that. If someone doesn’t like or is using your product you should refund. Their business plan is relying on people who forget to cancel after their trial!!!! Pathetic!

reviews.title: Another money sucking app
reviews.text:
Signed up for a trial period at £10 a month or so, then after having browsed the app I decided that it wasn’t worth it. I try to cancel my membership straight away, but was presented with a “if you cancel now, you won’t be able to keep records of your progress for the 3 months left on your membership. We suggest to keep it and we will warn you when your membership is about to renew so you would be able to cancel at that time.” Except that I never received a reminder from Liven and today they took £99 for an extra 3 month’s membership… well done guys, dark ux is the way to go for you. It’s a shame that those apps are relying on those recurring subscriptions to make some money. 
Plus the app was nothing worth £100 for 3 months. 
So if you discovered an app via a social portal which is heavily advertising, it’s probably some money grabbers.

reviews.title: Disjointed user experience too much commercial gamification
reviews.text: I was hoping paying for this app would mean a thoughtful user experience. Unfortunately it is really unclear how to use it effectively. There are lots of buttons and requests to log information or interact but the pathway is not very clear for the user seeking a self help course to support them. One minute you are journaling the next logging mood, they are non sequitur experiences. The best bit was the learning course but this was very text heavy . Unfortunately the whole experience was made worse by immediately highlighting additional services you can pay for -  monetisation felt heavy handed as did the Duolingo style recommitment to the course buttons interrupting the user flow. Really intrusive and inappropriate in both counts for a metal health app. sorry but I’m looking for a refund.

reviews.title: Scam!!!! Don’t use this app
reviews.text: WOULD BE GIVING 0 STARS IF YOU WERE ABLE TO DO SO BUT SINCE THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE I GUESS I HAVE TO GIVE ATLEAST 1 STAR TO BE ABLE TO LEAVE ANY KIND OF REVIEW. I Requested refund after less than 30 days of downloading this app and and forgetting to cancel my free trial membership and was charged multiple times in same month over $99 dollars then I tried to reach out to customer service and received a very dismissive response just explaining what was charged to me which I knew it was charged and I was requesting a refund just as the refund policy stated you could do in 30 days. Needless to say no one would help and refund policy is not true I plan on reporting you  to better business bureau as well as Apple’s customer care dept this company and app is very bad customer service and customer support. I’ve never been so disappointed with and treated so unfair and unkindly as well as treated by customer support in such a dismissive manner and they were very impolite and rude towards me and did not even try to assist me or find a possible way to help me or work with me. I was so very disappointed they are ALL ABOUT THE $$$   Super disappointed and will be sure to tell anyone who will listen or asks that this APP is terrible and unprofessionally run as a business….

reviews.title: Predatory
reviews.text:
I was trepidatious, I knew I was vulnerable to being taken advantage of by a subscription app. You guys have your targets in a barrel, ready to be shot, but I fell right for it.
ADHD is an illness, and people with it suffer. You guys are poised to exploit that. It's genius and I wish you didn't catch me in a moment of weakness. Because I knew what would happen, and then it did. Woke up today to messages of payments that didn't go through and a bank overdraft. Because my last ninety-something dollars went to this stupid app. It didn't help me at all - except to leave another burn mark. Then, trying to cancel. You make it confusing on purpose: you immediately sweep us away from accessing our account by placing us into an activity that it's impossible to skip, then use misleading "options" in response to redundant confirmatory "are you sure you wanna cancel?" questions.
You know what you're doing. Kudos to a job well-done. At every opportunity, you take advantage. I'm sure you're making tons of money. Sleep well.

reviews.title: Underwhelmed
reviews.text: It's not bad but after all the adverts saying it was a must have app I’m not exactly blown away. Some interesting stuff for sure and probably a 3 star if it wasn't for the hype curve downgrade. Considering it's a well being app turning off notifications for auto-renew feels a bit dirty. I get it but it's a bit anti-brand. Just says I'm in a bad mood or neutral, which is accurate but that seems to be fully linked to what I type not my facial scan. Offers me the same piece of advice every day, unless I pay more for expensive add-ons. Learning is interesting but not ground breaking, unless you pay more (I paid £25 for 12 weeks). I pressed to pause my account for 3 months and now i can't log in. I think it cancelled but have no idea 🤷 hoped for more, got more of the same.

reviews.title: Just a Cash Grab
reviews.text: This app is nothing more than an elaborate scam to get cash quick under the guise of mental health assistance. I was sold on a 3 month course catered to my needs. After paying for 3 months, what I got were two weeks worth of lessons and a fancy mood tracker. The “lessons” were more like 10 minute reads on Cognitive Behavioral Therapy that could have been procured from a Google search. There are no real exercises or involved work, just a bunch of articles. When I decided to cancel, they punished me by setting a 60 hour clock on wiping all my accumulated data in the app. I still have nearly two months left in the original subscription I paid for, but instead of clearing the data at the end they decide to do it now with no refund or pro-rated subscription return. Honestly, I feel like this is a scam, and I would recommend avoiding it. The benefits do not out-weigh the frustrations or cost.

reviews.title: Damaging
reviews.text: This experience felt unsafe. The practitioner made assumptions about me and my needs without asking me anything (simply read my information before the call - which is expected but very uncomfortable to have personal things discussed before we even did an introduction). The practitioner then launched into exercises without checking comfort or boundaries, further leading to my discomfort. When I ended the session because I felt uncomfortable, it was logged as a no-show, and I was then offered a free week’s subscription, which felt dismissive and inappropriate given the situation. This lacked professionalism and raised serious concerns about client safety and duty of care.

reviews.title: Brilliant but also disappointing
reviews.text:
I used the app for a month and it was excellent. The AI feature didn’t feel like AI most of the time, other than when it asked a question at the end of every answer. But it did feel like talking to a real person and the advice and conversations were super-helpful and insightful. 
However the experience was spoilt by Liven’s aggressive subscription model. For example they are not transparent about subscription fees. I have read lots about users who continued to be charged when they thought that they had cancelled. I couldn’t find a definitive breakdown of costs and felt patronised by the phrase, “The price of the Liven app adjusts gently based on the subscription option you choose. Discover a plan that beautifully aligns with your personal needs and aspirations.” 😮 Hippy nonsense and incredibly irritating too. I am disappointed that this is the case, particularly as the app itself is built around well-being and compassion. It seems that beneath the surface lurks the same cynical money-making model as everything else. Also a shame because the app is really good but it does now feel like I was being drawn into a cult.

reviews.title: Not helpful
reviews.text: I bought this app because I was looking for convenient place where I can do lists of things to do and plan them through the days/ weeks etc. Liven advertised such function. In reality the app had his own to do lists that were rigid and could not be exchanged to what YOU  really need. Nooo! instead of your goals one should use the goals someone else invented for you.  It s not user friendly, not intuitive, not convenient. I fought with it for a couple of days, wrote to support got some kind of explanation that did not help and gave up. Lost money and the lists I write as before on the list of paper. But at least these are my goals, not some unknown idiot.

reviews.title: Simplistic
reviews.text: I have tried Liven multiple times altho admittedly, I don't make it past 1-2 days. #1 bc I have ADHD memory loss. But perhaps more so #2 bc Liven is so simplistic, basic, top line, cheery sing songy (& heavily AI driven, so feels quite false). Does not dive into core issues for serious help. (despite promises in Ads to do just that.) I have been on Adderall max legal dose for 4yrs. No change. In fact, I think ADHD has gotten worse. (I cannot function at all: watching myself completely disappear & I dont know now if I will ever get better.) LIVEN MAKES BIG CLAIMS & magical promises. Yet it is too elemental & child like. It feels degrading. I need serious help. I know my ADHD symptoms very well, after 10yrs of research & chasing diagnosis. But Liven is like "Adhd101 Light: Beginners only" when I need actual assistance to move past the road blocks. Liven doesnt seem capable or even attempting to provide that level of help. Its at a cartoon coloring book level, when I need deep help at masterclass level.

reviews.title: Avoid!!! Expensive & awful customer service
reviews.text:
The app itself is good, the navigation is nice and the AI built in features are smart. 

The positive stops there I’m afraid. After you try your free trial & delete the app(asking for the subscription to be changed as you delete) the subscription will not in fact stop 

Liven subscription automatically renews to a extortionate £50 a month, no reminders are sent they just continue to take funds. 

After I stopped using liven I found a free tool funding by the nhs which by the way is FREE and better than liven hence my disbelief (How we feel) 

I spoke with liven and requested a refund, they offered to refund a month but not all the other months they had taken money because “its policy” I repeatedly explained the circumstances and asked for it to be escalated -the agent didn’t listen (clearly AI support) as the whole thing was non empathetic and dismissive , sending me links and quoting me by the wrong name . 

Whilst the app is good it’s not that good and much better free tools out there - save yourself the money and the awful experience - don’t be fooled by the nice fancy marketing on the campaign

reviews.title: Bait and switch
reviews.text: I really didn’t like that the app has a paid subscription AFTER getting me through the onboarding. I feel like that is bait and switch tactic and the last thing I should have to worry about when signing up for help with mental health. You make the user feel vulnerable and get them to go through a big process where I have to invest time and get promises from your app about how much better my life will be and then I have to pay to actually get that stuff. It’s disgusting honestly. I’m an app developer and I understand that you need to get paid but that is a scummy tactic. Just tell the user upfront that they will have to pay. Don’t get me hooked and then tell me I have to pay an ABSURDLY high amount. $8 a week is insane. If I can get lifetime access for $100 the maybe the app shouldn’t be free but it should be $100 in the store. Find a better way to onboard your users without bait and switch. And offer a reasonable price tier for folks that aren’t rich. Your app is only for rich people. Are rich folks the only ones that need mental health? It’s absolutely insane. I’m on Medicaid and food stamps. You think I can afford $8 a week? That’s so disrespectful to poor people. They don’t deserve help from you. Smh. You know what you’re doing. Fix it.

reviews.title: Boring
reviews.text: Got swayed by late night scrolling when I was feeling particularly down, believed it was a 7 day free trial but was charged £20 for a month, quickly ended the subscription before it charges me £50 going forward!. All it is is quizzes and articles - chat GTP and Google could get you the same information. Was hoping for fresh content, videos and audio sounds to soothe the nervous system. Maybe one video article in the last 1.5weeks. Also they have a streak count so if you are already overwhelmed don’t bother as it just becomes another thing to achieve and tick off daily. Bummed I lost £20 on this

reviews.title: Be careful
reviews.text:
Not worth the money at all. Liven requires you to commit to three months upfront, which feels incredibly restrictive—especially once you realize how little value the platform actually provides. The services and tools offered are very basic, generic, and easily found elsewhere for free or at a much lower cost. There’s nothing innovative or premium about the content, and it feels like a lot of surface-level guidance packaged as something transformational.

The app promises support, structure, and improvement, but in reality, it delivers vague suggestions, repetitive content, and minimal personalization. The experience feels automated rather than genuinely helpful, and there’s no meaningful accountability or depth that would justify the price. For what you’re paying, you’d expect robust resources, expert-level insights, or real customization—none of which are present.

To make matters worse, even after canceling, I was still charged, which adds to the overall negative experience. Having to chase down billing issues after already feeling disappointed by the service is frustrating and unacceptable. Between the forced upfront commitment, underwhelming offerings, and billing problems, Liven comes across as overpriced and misleading.
